title: F2 Loop Round Behavior
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be finite Boolean Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose a mode, an input word, words $s$, $s'$, $p$, and $w$, a Boolean acceptance value, a configuration of $F$, and a positive integer $t$. Suppose that, starting from the configuration with state $a$ and tape contents given by placing $s$ on tape $0$ and leaving the other tapes blank, the run of $B$ never visits state $a$ at any time strictly between $0$ and $t$. Suppose also that at time $t$ the run has halted with output $p$ if it is accepted, and otherwise is exactly the configuration with state $a$ and tape contents given by placing $s'$ on tape $0$ and leaving the other tapes blank. Then the loop host, started from the corresponding call configuration with the given word $w$ and fuel configuration, reaches within $3t+2|w|+5$ steps either a halted configuration whose output is $p$ in find mode and $[\mathrm{true}]$ otherwise (in the accepted case); the next call configuration with word equal to the debit of $w$ (if the run was not accepted and the debit reports success); or a halted configuration with output $[]$ in find mode and $[\mathrm{false}]$ otherwise (if the run was not accepted and the debit reports failure).
hypotheses_covered: No visit to $a$ at times $u$ with $0<u<t$ in the run from the seam configuration for $s$
At time $t$, acceptance means the machine is halted with output $p$
At time $t$, nonacceptance means the configuration is the seam configuration for $s'$
